summary: Six-round independent adversarial review (fresh-context Opus agents, read-only) of the #488 watch-party guest drift-rebuild fix. Round 1: caught that an early draft reused needsHlsSessionRebuild's forward/buffered-edge arm, causing rebuild storms on session boot/thin-buffer/end-of-title — removed, replaced with a narrower needsBackwardSessionRebuild covering only the reported backward-anchor case. Round 2: core predicate/units/host-guard/tests clean; fixed inaccurate comments, added target/anchor clamping and a 1s tolerance. Round 3: found a real medium regression — the rebuild's only content guard (partyMediaItemId, series-level) couldn't see a TV-show episode advance, risking a spurious rebuild of the wrong episode; fixed with isPartyEpisodeMismatch + a new partyEpisodeId field threaded through PartySync/App.tsx. Round 4: found that fix itself read a stale closure (partyEpisodeId wasn't in the effect's dep array); fixed by reading through the existing partySyncRef live-ref pattern already used elsewhere in the file for this purpose — recommended NO-GO until fixed, then re-reviewed. Round 5: explicit GO, zero critical/high across all rounds; two prescribed low-severity follow-ups (isPartyEpisodeMismatch needed != null since the wire value for a no-episode party is JSON null, not undefined; a doc comment misattributed the reachable scenario) — both applied. Round 6: explicit GO, verified the null-fix and comment corrections independently against server marshaling code and App.tsx, zero critical/high/medium; four low/nitpick findings (a type-honesty gap on PartySync.partyEpisodeId, a dead fallback in a rev chain, a playbackRate-reset omission matching a pre-existing neighbor, minor comment imprecision) — the actionable one (type honesty) applied in a final compiler-verified, zero-behavior-change commit not itself re-reviewed given its mechanical nature. Build/lint/660 vitest tests green throughout.
